lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Remove both date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are unnecessary, create privacy and bias concerns, and use valuable space.

items.because: It is vague, reads as promotional language, and lacks a concrete action, scope, user count, baseline, and measurable result.

items.says: Clarify whether 35% is a relative improvement or a percentage-point increase, identify the baseline and evaluation set or case count, define 'diagnostic accuracy', clarify what 'validated' means, and ensure assistant-only masking was materially responsible.
Clarify the causal link between the branch and the 68% reduction, state the backlog baseline or approximate case volume, explain '800+ sensor signals', and clarify production status.
Replace 'by 4x' with an unambiguous reduction expression, provide before-and-after memory figures, clarify impact on throughput/training/model quality, and specify model scope.
Add missing grammatical prepositions, use consistent U.S. spelling, state evaluation scale, define redundant tool calls, clarify SFT baseline, and consider jargon density.
Clarify how reviewer disagreement was measured, over how many cases, whether lower disagreement meant greater correctness, and reduce ambiguity around 'in-scope signals'.
Clarify how citation quality was scored, how many evaluation cases were involved, and distinguish between regressions detected and prevented.

Fix tense mismatch ('Maintained' and 'adds'), clarify whether release cycles were shortened to or by three days, add previous duration, ensure verb reflects ownership, and specify regression check coverage.
Clarify whether all 30 were independently scheduled services or jobs within fewer services, and add a measurable reliability or operational result if available.
Clarify tested request volume, concurrency, or production traffic, confirm no compromise to data freshness or correctness, and make CI load test explicit if applicable.
Replace 'Owner' with a more precise role, add a project link if public, verify start date is not future-dated, and standardize category formatting.
Explain how the 100-turn stress test was constructed, clarify 'raw conversation grew 100x', state if information retention was measured, and define 'budgeted context layers' and 'staged compaction'.
Clarify whether deadlocks and lost results were observed in production, integration, or stress testing, state trial/failure rates, clarify '50-way fan-out', and consider reducing jargon.
Add a repository or project link if public.
Clarify whether the contribution was merged and released, specify implementation details, and mention test coverage or reproducibility if relevant.
Specify which Kendall statistic was used, clarify degradation generation, number of systems/reports/conditions, aggregation of 0.89, and describe perturbations.
Move Git out of programming-language category, add only languages you can use confidently, and include SQL only if proficient.
Separate frameworks, training methods, and expertise areas, use a more specific skill category than 'agent evaluation', include SFT if applicable, and add infrastructure tools only if used.
Use consistent date punctuation and ensure 'Expected' is not mistaken for part of the degree title.
Replace generic country/location placeholders and use the same date style as the graduate degree line.

Use one spelling convention throughout, use past tense for completed roles, standardize hyphens, date formats, commas, and capitalization, prevent line breaks splitting compounds, check PDF text extraction, and avoid repeating achievements.
